title.narrative: Pilot project to strengthen agricultural production and processing as strategies for income generation and poverty reduction in Choc and Antioquia

description.narrative: Afro-Colombian communities living in the Medio Atrato region of Choc and Antioquia rely on agriculture and agro-forestry for their food needs and livelihoods yet often lack basic inputs and technical skills necessary to fully develop their collective lands. The IAF supports community-led solutions to increasing economic inclusion and opportunities through sustainable agriculture and natural resource management practices. Our grantee partner Asociacin De Productores Del Medio Atrato (ASPRODEMA) strengthens four value chains that are vital to farming communities along Colombia?s Pacific coast: rice peach palm plantain and sugar cane. ASPRODEMA also supports community-based businesses and marketing of value-added products like sugar cane syrup and plantain flour to promote food security and economic self-sufficiency. Amendment FY19:This amendment provides ASPRODEMA with an additional $31,692 to ensure the grantee is properly staffed in order to continue strengthening agricultural value chains and community-based businesses in the Medio Atrato region of Choc and Antioquia, Colombia. Amendment FY21: This amendment provides ASPRODEMA with an additional $19,570 to address the effects of Hurricanes Eta and Iota and subsequent weather events as well as the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. ASPRODEMA is distributing food baskets and seeds to participants whose farming plots were washed away by flooding. It is also providing additional agricultural, environmental, and management training to local technical committees whose work was interrupted by both emergencies. ASPRODEMA is designing and implementing biosecurity protocols for staff and participants to use during field visits and implementing virtual technical assistance during stay-at-home orders.This amendment is part of the IAF's broader Eta/Iota and COVID-19 response strategies.
